etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin sexuālis, from sexus (“sex”), equivalent to sex +‎ -ual.

definitions.definition: Arising from the fact of being male or female; pertaining to sex or gender, or to the social relations between the sexes. [from 17th c.]
(biology) Capable of sexual reproduction; sexed, sexuate. [from 19th c.]
Pertaining to sexual intercourse or other intimate physical contact. [from 18th c.]

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Mark Tran, “Denied an education by war”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 1:
quote.text: One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on schools […] as children, teachers or school buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to school. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.

definitions.definition: Characterised by sexual feelings or behaviour; possessing sexuality. [from 19th c.]

quote.text: We don't often think of Jesus as a sexual person, but He certainly was not asexual. He was not just God on earth. He was fully human and  […]  He was sexual, single, and celibate.

definitions.definition: Pertaining to sexuality as a cultural phenomenon; relating to sexual behaviour or conduct. [from 19th c.]
(LGBTQ, of a person, rare) Experiencing sexual attraction; not asexual.

quote.citation: 2016, Kyell Gold, Black Angel, Kyell Gold, →ISBN:
quote.text: […]  “You know, there are asexuals with sexual partners.” His ears flicked, and he grinned. “There's things both of us can try to do […] ”

quote.citation: 2017, T. T. Monday, Double Switch, Vintage Crime/Black Lizard, →ISBN, page 98:
quote.text: Izzy tells me that at her high school the most useful distinction is not between heterosexuals and homosexuals but between those who are sexual and those who are not. The abstainers call themselves “aces,” short for “asexuals.”

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Pertaining to the female sex. [17th–19th c.]

quote.citation: 1791 (date written), Mary Wollstonecraft, “Observations on the State of Degradation to which Woman is Reduced by Various Causes”, in A Vindication of the Rights of Woman: With Strictures on Political and Moral Subjects, London:  […]  J[oseph] Johnson, […], published 1792, →OCLC, page 112:
quote.text: [T]he inquiry is whether she have reason or not. If she have, which, for a moment, I will take for granted, she was not created merely to be the solace of man, and the sexual should not destroy the human character.

definitions.definition: (biology) A species which reproduces by sexual rather than asexual reproduction, or a member of such a species.
(LGBTQ) A person who experiences sexual attraction, a person who has interest in or desire for sex (especially as contrasted with an asexual).

quote.citation: 2012, Issues in Sexuality and Sexual Behavior Research: 2011 Edition, ScholarlyEditions, →ISBN:
quote.text: The findings suggest that asexuality is best conceptualized as a lack of sexual attraction; however, asexuals varied greatly in their experience of sexual  response and behavior. Asexuals partnered with sexuals acknowledged having to 'negotiate' sexual activity.

quote.citation: 2015, Mark Carrigan, Kristina Gupta, Todd G. Morrison, Asexuality and Sexual Normativity: An Anthology, Routledge, →ISBN, page 11:
quote.text: In this article we use absence of sexual attraction to others as a definition but recognise that this definition is contested.  […]  [A survey] was also advertised  online (without explicitly mentioning asexuality in the advert), thus aiming to reach a mixture of asexuals and sexuals.
